spacing.notes: Most frequent: 2.5px (42), 5px (41), 10px (39), 15px (32). Section gaps 130px between feature blocks, 455-536px around the hero and product demo.

colors.role: surface / product frame fill (57.7% of painted area)
single accent: primary button + footer slab only

taste.name: Headline at reading size
taste.trigger: When introducing the product above the fold
taste.decision: Chose a 19.2px regular-weight h1 that is the same size as the section titles over a 48-72px display headline
taste.reason: Because a visitor who is addressed at reading volume reads a sentence instead of scanning a slogan; nothing is shouted, so nothing feels sold
evidence: h1 19.2px/400 and h2 19.2px/700: hierarchy by weight only

taste.name: One accent, spent twice
taste.trigger: When choosing where colour may appear on a grey-and-white page
taste.decision: Chose a single dark navy (#00075F) for the primary button and the footer slab only, over tinting links, icons or section backgrounds
taste.reason: Because when colour appears in exactly one interactive place, the eye finds the next step without being told
evidence: #00075F: 3 elements, 11% of painted area, all of it footer
every other surface is pure grey #F7F7F7/#EDEDED/#DEDEDE
secondary button is #F7F7F7 fill with no border

taste.name: Proof that is computed, not claimed
taste.trigger: When showing longevity and community size
taste.decision: Chose an inline bold running counter ('N years and N days') and an exact member count inside prose over stat tiles, logo walls or testimonials
taste.reason: Because an exact, odd number set in a sentence reads as a fact somebody measured; a rounded '10k+' tile reads as marketing
evidence: hero sentence with bold duration, weight 700 inside 19.2px body
exact supporter count inside the mission-section prose
no logo wall, no star ratings on the page

taste.name: Short, decelerating motion
taste.trigger: When adding hover and state transitions
taste.decision: Chose 150-240ms opacity/transform transitions on an expo-out curve over long springy or scroll-triggered entrances
taste.reason: Because motion that finishes before the finger leaves the trackpad feels like response, not performance
